Summary Method for an Object of Class betanb

Source: R/betaNB-beta-nb-methods.R
summary.betanb.Rd

Summary Method for an Object of Class betanb

Usage

# S3 method for class 'betanb'
summary(object, alpha = NULL, type = "pc", digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

object

Object of Class betanb, that is, the output of the BetaNB(), RSqNB(), SCorNB(), DeltaRSqNB(), PCorNB(), FSqNB(), or DiffBetaNB() functions.

alpha

Numeric vector. Significance level \(\alpha\). If alpha = NULL, use the argument alpha used in object.

type

Character string. Confidence interval type, that is, type = "pc" for percentile; type = "bc" for bias corrected; type = "bca" for bias corrected and accelerated; type = "mpc" for modified percentile, available only for DeltaRSqNB() (unadjusted or adj = TRUE).

digits

Digits to print.

...

additional arguments.

Value

Returns a matrix of estimates, standard errors, number of bootstrap replications, and confidence intervals.

Details

Let \(\hat{\theta}\) be the estimate, \(\hat{\theta}^{\ast}_{1}, \dots, \hat{\theta}^{\ast}_{R}\) the bootstrap draws with empirical distribution function \(\hat{G}\), \(\Phi\) the standard normal distribution function, and \(z_{p} = \Phi^{-1} \left( p \right)\). The limits of a \(100 \left( 1 - \alpha \right) \%\) interval are \(\hat{G}^{-1} \left( p_{1} \right)\) and \(\hat{G}^{-1} \left( p_{2} \right)\) (type 7 quantiles of the draws). The percentile interval (type = "pc") uses \(p_{1} = \alpha / 2\) and \(p_{2} = 1 - \alpha / 2\). The bias-corrected interval (type = "bc") uses $$p_{k} = \Phi \left( 2 \hat{z}_{0} + z_{\alpha_{k}} \right), \quad \hat{z}_{0} = \Phi^{-1} \left( \frac{1}{R} \sum_{b = 1}^{R} I \left( \hat{\theta}^{\ast}_{b} < \hat{\theta} \right) \right),$$ where \(I\) is the indicator function, \(\alpha_{1} = \alpha / 2\), and \(\alpha_{2} = 1 - \alpha / 2\). The bias-corrected and accelerated interval (type = "bca") uses $$p_{k} = \Phi \left( \hat{z}_{0} + \frac{\hat{z}_{0} + z_{\alpha_{k}}}{1 - \hat{a} \left( \hat{z}_{0} + z_{\alpha_{k}} \right)} \right), \quad \hat{a} = \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^{n} \left( \bar{\theta}_{\left( \cdot \right)} - \hat{\theta}_{\left( -i \right)} \right)^{3}}{6 \left[ \sum_{i = 1}^{n} \left( \bar{\theta}_{\left( \cdot \right)} - \hat{\theta}_{\left( -i \right)} \right)^{2} \right]^{3 / 2}},$$ where \(\hat{\theta}_{\left( -i \right)}\) is the jackknife estimate without observation \(i\) and \(\bar{\theta}_{\left( \cdot \right)}\) is their mean (Efron & Tibshirani, 1993). Failed draws are dropped. The modified percentile interval (type = "mpc") is described in DeltaRSqNB().

References

Efron, B., & Tibshirani, R. J. (1993). An introduction to the bootstrap. Chapman & Hall. doi:10.1201/9780429246593

Author

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Examples

# Data ---------------------------------------------------------------------
data("nas1982", package = "betaNB")

# Fit Model in lm ----------------------------------------------------------
object <- stats::lm(
  formula = QUALITY ~ NARTIC + PCTGRT + PCTSUPP,
  data = nas1982
)

# NB -----------------------------------------------------------------------
nb <- NB(
  object = object,
  R = 100, # use a large value e.g., 5000L for actual research
  seed = 0508
)

# BetaNB -------------------------------------------------------------------
out <- BetaNB(object = nb, alpha = 0.05)

## Methods -----------------------------------------------------------------
summary(object = out)
#> Call:
#> BetaNB(object = nb, alpha = 0.05)
#> 
#> Standardized regression slopes
#> type = "pc"
#>            est     se   R   2.5%  97.5%
#> NARTIC  0.4951 0.0708 100 0.3498 0.6141
#> PCTGRT  0.3915 0.0797 100 0.2440 0.5192
#> PCTSUPP 0.2632 0.0813 100 0.1033 0.4193
